headline: Talent is natural aptitude—a head start that still requires practice to develop fully
universal_truth: Talent sets the slope, practice climbs the hill; both matter, but only practice is in your control
fun_facts: Even Mozart practiced intensively—his early works were mostly arrangements, not original compositions
Studies show that by age 20, elite musicians have practiced about 10,000 hours more than average ones
Natural talent accounts for roughly 25% of performance differences—the rest is training
discussion_questions: What natural abilities do you have?
How have you developed or neglected your talents?
When do you let lack of natural talent become an excuse?

hook.script: Some people seem naturally gifted—they learn faster, pick up skills easily. But even prodigies practice. Talent is a head start, not a finish line. Raw ability still requires development.

cliff.script: The talent vs. practice debate rages in sports, arts, and academics. What's the actual relationship?
cliff.prompt: How do talent and practice relate?

options.text: Talent sets the slope, practice climbs the hill—natural ability determines learning rate, but practice determines distance traveled; untrained talent loses to trained mediocrity
options.response: Yes. Talent helps you learn faster, but without practice, it stays potential. Practiced modest talent usually beats unpracticed high talent. Both matter; only one is in your control.
Talent matters, but research shows practice accounts for most performance differences...

fact1.title: Head Start, Not Finish Line
fact1.script: Talent gives you a head start—you learn faster in that domain. But a head start doesn't win races without running them. Practice is still required.

fact2.title: Talent Identification
fact2.script: Finding your talents matters—where do you learn unusually fast? Where does effort yield unusual results? Those are signs of natural aptitude worth developing.

fact3.title: The Control Question
fact3.script: You can't control your talents—they're given. You can control your practice—that's chosen. Focus on what you control. Develop what you have.

wisdom.script: Here's today's wisdom: Talent sets the slope, practice climbs the hill. Both matter, but only practice is in your control. Develop what you have.

outro.script: That's Day 293. Tomorrow, we'll explore how we know what's true—evidence. Until then, consider your natural talents and how you're developing them.

growTrack.title: Talent Development - What Are You Building On?
growTrack.learning_objective: Identify natural talents and plan their development
growTrack.activity: Where do you learn faster than others? Where does effort yield unusual results? Those are your talents. Are you developing them, or letting them sit as untrained potential?
